geometry: dendritic branching to a fixed ratio
solving_for: delivery of a fluid to every point of a fixed enclosed volume

constraints.name: enclosing volume, fixed and uniform, known in advance
constraints.note: the second term. Where it exists it fixes the branching exponent; the lung's is 2^(-1/3)

constraints.name: work lost per unit delivered
constraints.note: stated as dissipation in joules, not as a cost — cost imports a pricing model that is not part of the system being read

why_not_the_other_geometry.note: nothing is rotating, so there is no term to wind the delivery path. Flux across a boundary under dissipation branches; rotation plus infall spirals

removal_test.absent_in: a river network — there is no enclosing volume to fill, so the second term is absent
removal_test.observed_form: deltas, rather than branching to a fixed ratio

scale_index.characteristic_scale: capillary diameter — the scale at which the branching stops and delivery becomes diffusive

note: the fit describes the surviving sample; what carries the weight is the recurrence list, and the exponent is a label on it

provenance.note: the read, both worked examples and the recurrence list are quoted from SHAPE_SPEC.md sections 3, 4, 6 and 9. The scale index was written during the build

solving_for: distribution of matter across an extent

constraints.name: angular momentum of the infalling material
constraints.note: rotation plus infall winds the distribution path

why_not_the_other_geometry.note: both distribute across an extent, so asking why the galaxy is not dendritic is what locates the term. The missing variable was found by the question, not by inspection

removal_test.absent_in: vasculature — flux across a boundary under dissipation, with nothing rotating

scale_index.characteristic_scale: the disc scale length, below which the rotation curve no longer sets the form

provenance.note: the read and the recovered term are quoted from SHAPE_SPEC.md section 3. The scale index and the recurrence list were written during the build and are the fields to check first

geometry: branching where the substrate yields, routing around where it does not
solving_for: discharge of sediment and water into a receiving basin

constraints.name: whatever substrate was hit — hardened rock the flow cannot cut
constraints.note: the boundary was not chosen by the system. The geometry is a record of the substrate, and reading it as an optimum reads a transcript of terrain as a solution

constraints.name: sediment supplied against subsidence and wave energy

why_not_the_other_geometry.other_geometry: branching to a fixed ratio, as in a lung
why_not_the_other_geometry.recovered_term: the absent enclosure, and the heterogeneity of the boundary
why_not_the_other_geometry.note: there is no enclosing volume to fill and the boundary is not uniform, so neither term that fixes an exponent is present

removal_test.absent_in: a delta prograding onto uniform unconsolidated sediment
removal_test.observed_form: unrecorded — the comparison has not been made here

scale_index.characteristic_scale: the avulsion length — the distance a channel runs before it switches

note: kept as a marker rather than tested: the removal test is stated and has not been run, which is the difference between a stated boundary and a measured one

provenance.note: the delta-meeting-hardened-rock case and the supply/removal ratio are quoted from SHAPE_SPEC.md sections 5 and 9. The removal test, scale index and recurrence list were written during the build
